name: Closed-transition transfer switch
summary: A transfer switch that briefly parallels two synchronised sources so the load moves without interruption.
description: A closed-transition transfer switch connects the load to the new source before disconnecting it from the old one, with both sources paralleled for a short time, typically less than 100 milliseconds. A synchronism check confirms that voltage, frequency and phase angle are within limits before the overlap is allowed.

Drawings show two switching devices or a transfer switch with both contacts able to close, plus a synchronism check function and often a note on maximum overlap time. Where the overlap is longer than the network operator allows, a soft-load transfer with a paralleling controller is used instead.

Even a momentary parallel connection can require approval from the network operator and protection against the generator feeding a utility fault. The symbol does not show the overlap timer, its backup trip or the interface protection.
readingNotes: A synchronism check function should be associated with the switch.
Read the maximum overlap time permitted.
drawingChecklist: State overlap time and synchronising limits.
Show synchronism check and backup trip.
distinction: A closed-transition switch overlaps the two sources; an open-transition switch always breaks before it makes.
